text.p: Walgreen Co. said Monday that earnings rose 18 percent in its fourth quarter, boosted by strength in its pharmacy business and robust sales of general merchandise at its drug stores.

Net earnings rose to $89.7 million, or 36 cents a share, in the quarter ended on Aug. 31, from $76.3 million, or 31 cents a share, in the 1995 quarter. Sales grew 13.6 percent to $2.92 billion from $2.57 billion.
The results, which included a gain related to inventory accounting equal to 1 cent a share, matched expectations on Wall Street.
For the year, earnings rose 16 percent to a record, the 22nd consecutive year of record results, the Deerfield, Ill.-based drug store chain said.
President L. Daniel Jorndt said general merchandise sales were excellent and that sales at stores open at least a year rose 8.8 percent for the quarter and 8.5 percent for the year.
Prescription sales at Walgreen pharmacy departments grew 16.9 percent for the quarter and 18 percent for the year.
"Walgreens -- with nearly 190 million prescriptions filled in 1996 -- is the largest and fastest growing retail prescription provider in America," Jorndt said in a statement.
A new system to speed prescription-filling was scheduled to be in all stores by next spring, he said.
Walgreen opened 210 new drugstores in fiscal 1996, the most ever in one year, and plans to open 230 new units for fiscal 1997, it said.
As of Aug. 31, the company had 2,193 drug stores in 34 states and Puerto Rico, compared with 2,085 a year ago.
For the full year, Walgreen earned $371.7 million, or $1.50 a share, up from $320.8 million, or $1.30 a share, in fiscal 1995. Sales grew 13 percent to $11.78 billion from $10.40 billion.
Walgreen stock lost 25 cents to $36.875 in morning trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
